newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PSE PLANS TO REQUIRE IAS COMPANY RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PSE PLANS TO REQUIRE IAS COMPANY RESULTS.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange said on Tuesday it would require companies with stock listed on the bourse to file earnings results under international accounting standards (IAS) once a new markets watchdog takes office.

"In the (proposed) law about the Securities Commission is a paragraph which will require issuers to submit financial results according to international standards," the PSE chamber's chairman, Tomas Jezek, told a news conference.
Czech companies, except for larger firms usually with shares or debt instruments traded abroad, file results only according to Czech accounting standards which remain the requirement for the PSE.
IAS rules differ from Czech accounting in areas such as depreciation writeoffs, leasing payments and measuring profits and losses carried over from previous years.

Jezek and the PSE have been actively pursuing the creation of a new independent markets watchdog modelled on the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), after years of criticism of Finance Ministry oversight.

Jezek said he expected a draft law setting up the new commission to be submitted to both the Finance Ministry and the parliament within the next 10 days, aiming for the legislation to win approval and the commission to begin work by July 1.
